How to ask, and what this tutor will and will not do

Name the idea, or name the exercise. One sentence is enough. You do not need to be polite or formal — you need to be specific. "In PA06 Exercise 3, why is the empty set a subset?" works; "sets??" does not.

It knows this course, and nothing else. Your lecture slides, your practice assignments and their solutions, and past exams and quizzes. Every answer was written in advance by your instructor. Nothing here is invented at the moment you ask, and when the tutor is not confident it says so instead of answering anyway.

You will not be given a full solution on the first request. Take three hints, or post what you have tried — a few honest lines — and the answer opens straight away. Reading a solution feels like learning and is not; the mark you get comes from what you can do with a blank page. Explanations, definitions and questions about the course are never withheld.

Model answers to past exams are not published here. The solution files kept beside the old papers are incomplete, and in places belong to questions that were later replaced. Instead you are pointed to the practice exercises that use the same ideas, whose solutions were written to be published and are reliable.

Please write in English. Academic English is a skill this degree expects of you, and a clearly expressed question gets a more reliable answer.

If nothing matches, send the question to Dr Ashry with the button that appears. Questions collected that way get proper answers added to the tutor, often within the week.

Answers come from this course's own material. Nothing here is generated by an AI at the moment you ask — every answer was written in advance.
